While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Oregon’s Painted Hills are rounded clay hills marked by distinctive red, yellow, tan, and black bands.
• The bands began as volcanic ash deposited by eruptions about 30 to 40 million years ago.
• Each ash layer gradually weathered into soil before subsequent eruptions buried it.
• The minerals that formed in each soil depended on the prevailing climate.
• Warm, humid conditions produced iron-rich red soils, while cooler, drier conditions produced yellowish and tan soils.
items.stem: The student wants to explain why the bands of the Painted Hills differ in color. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Because each band began as ash from a different volcanic eruption, the bands of the Painted Hills contain different minerals and therefore show different colors.
The red bands of the Painted Hills formed during cooler, drier periods, whereas the yellowish and tan bands formed when the climate was warm and humid.
Each band of the Painted Hills is a former soil that developed from ash under a particular climate, which determined the band’s minerals and thus its color.
Deposited by eruptions about 30 to 40 million years ago, the volcanic ash in the Painted Hills gradually weathered into soil, layer by layer.
items.explanation: The goal is to explain why the bands differ in color. The notes link three facts: each ash layer “gradually weathered into soil,” the minerals in each soil “depended on the prevailing climate,” and those minerals set the color (“Warm, humid conditions produced iron-rich red soils, while cooler, drier conditions produced yellowish and tan soils”). Choice C joins them: each band formed under its own climate, which fixed its minerals and so its color.

A.why_wrong: It gives a reason for the colors, but the notes tie each soil’s minerals to the prevailing climate, not to which eruption produced the ash.

B.why_wrong: It links color to climate but reverses the notes: red soils formed in warm, humid conditions, and yellowish and tan soils in cooler, drier ones.

D.recipe: PART (how the layers formed, not why they differ)
D.why_wrong: It explains how the ash became layers of soil, but it never mentions climate or minerals, so it does not explain why the bands differ in color.

items.notes: Subject: natural science (geology of the Painted Hills, John Day Fossil Beds, Oregon). Real subject known without a search; no named people (WAVE.md: no fact-checking for this skill). Option fact check: A FALSE goal-shaped (eruption instead of climate), B FALSE goal-shaped (climates reversed), D true but partial. Goal-only solve (without the notes): A, B and C all explain the colors.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Fleets from Europe and North America fished for cod on the Grand Banks, off Newfoundland, for nearly five centuries.
• Beginning in the 1950s, industrial trawlers dragged enormous nets across the banks and froze their catch onboard.
• Catches soared for two decades, but fish were being caught faster than they could reproduce.
• In 1992, with the northern cod stock near collapse, Canada imposed a moratorium on commercial fishing.
• The moratorium eliminated tens of thousands of jobs, and the stock has recovered only partially since.
items.stem: The student wants to provide an overview of the history of the Grand Banks cod fishery. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: For nearly five centuries, industrial trawlers caught Grand Banks cod faster than the fish could reproduce, until Canada imposed a moratorium in 1992 from which the stock has only partially recovered.
Canada’s 1992 moratorium on commercial fishing, which eliminated tens of thousands of jobs, pushed the Grand Banks cod stock to near collapse after five centuries of fishing.
Beginning in the 1950s, industrial trawlers that froze their catch onboard enabled fleets to catch cod on the Grand Banks faster than the fish could reproduce.
Fished for centuries, the Grand Banks cod were driven to the brink of collapse by decades of industrial trawling; Canada halted commercial fishing in 1992, but the stock has never fully recovered.
items.explanation: An overview has to span the whole history: centuries of fishing, the trawler era, the near collapse and the 1992 moratorium, and the slow recovery. Choice D covers every stage and gets each link right: cod were fished for “nearly five centuries,” industrial trawlers arriving “Beginning in the 1950s” caught fish “faster than they could reproduce,” the stock fell “near collapse,” Canada “imposed a moratorium on commercial fishing,” and the stock “has recovered only partially since.”

A.recipe: FALSE (goal-shaped: trawling stretched over five centuries)
A.why_wrong: It spans the whole history, but it gives the five centuries of fishing to industrial trawlers; the notes say the trawlers arrived only “Beginning in the 1950s,” after nearly five centuries of fishing by earlier fleets.

B.why_wrong: It spans the history but reverses cause and effect: the stock was already near collapse when Canada imposed the moratorium, so the moratorium did not push it there.

C.why_wrong: It describes only the trawler era and why catches outpaced reproduction; the long history before it, the moratorium and its aftermath are missing.

items.notes: Subject: history and environmental science (collapse of the northern cod fishery). Real event known without a search; figures kept general (five centuries, tens of thousands of jobs); no named people. items.stem: The student wants to describe how a salt glaze forms on a pot. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

items.explanation: The goal is to describe how the glaze forms, so the sentence must follow the process in the notes: salt is added to the hot kiln, “The salt vaporizes, and sodium from the vapor combines with silica in the clay’s surface,” producing the glassy coating.
